context: Falcon prefetch histogram demo showing 500K synthetic events with an interactive brush on a daily timeline, a log-scaled value distribution histogram, and a latency comparison sparkline between O(1) cumulative-histogram lookup vs. O(N) naive scan.
first_impression: Structurally honest and well-engineered: zero baselines throughout, data-driven domains, and the histogram Y-axis is deliberately pinned to the full-dataset max so axes don't jump during brush filtering.
what_works: Zero baselines on both the area chart (y0=oH, domain starts at 0) and the bar histogram (dY.domain([0, d3.max(fullHist)])); the fixed full-dataset Y-domain during filtered rendering correctly satisfies the Subset Relation — remaining bars stay visually stable when the brush narrows the selection. Log-scaled bin edges with equal log-width intervals are appropriate for the tri-modal log-normal data and are honestly labeled.
what_doesnt: No .defined() guard on the timeline area/line generators — benign here because all 366 day slots are pre-allocated, but the pattern is fragile if data ever has gaps. The latency sparkline uses d3.scaleLog() but clamps values to lY.domain()[0] = 0.001 rather than surfacing true sub-millisecond readings, which can visually compress extremely fast prefetch times and understate the speedup magnitude.
